messages:
alex: heads-up — saw a customer report where a streaming request + tool call ended up being charged twice after a reconnect. looks like route affinity broke while the toolcall TTL was still live. :grimacing:
maria: can you paste the minimal logs/repro? which route switch happened? primary -> fallback?
alex: yep primary->fallback. short log: ```
INFO route=primary request_id=abc123 tool_call_id=tc-9ff ttl=30s tokens_charged=42
WARN connection=lost reconnecting... new_route=fallback request_id=abc123 tool_call_id=tc-9ff tokens_charged=0
INFO toolcall_expired tool_call_id=tc-9ff ttl_remaining=2s
INFO fallback served tokens_charged=42
```
alex: net result: billing ledger shows two 42-token entries (primary provisional + fallback confirmed). the provisional never reconciled away.
samir: that matches an edge where provisional credits are attributed to the original route, but on reconnect the fallback emits a confirmed charge without dedup. we need a canonical owner for the toolcall session across route handoffs.
maria: is the session id stable across the reconnect? request_id looks identical but router rewrote route tag.
julie: UX ask: console should surface "provisional vs confirmed" tokens per route so ops can see these transient duplicates. right now dashboard only shows rolled-up consumption and it's impossible to spot provisional leakage. :eyes: 
ben: telemetry-wise we should emit an event when provisional credits exist for > grace_window (30s). add a metric like `billing.provisional_stale_count` with route, model, and trace_id tags. that will let us alert and find customers impacted.
alex: agreed. quick mitigation: make ledger writes idempotent keyed by `tool_call_id` + `session_origin` so fallback can't double-write if the same tool_call_id shows up within TTL. but watch out for replays where a legitimately new toolcall reuses ids.
samir: another option: prefer move-to-confirmed instead of write-new-confirmed when a matching provisional exists. i.e., update provisional row to confirmed and include route ancestry. cheaper and avoids duplicates.
julie: product question: will that break provisioning metrics for dedicated vs hosted routes? we need to keep per-route accounting for SLA and chargeback. maybe keep confirmed row but keep `original_route` metadata. console can show lineage.
ben: +1 to lineage. Also we should add a small UI toggle: "show provisional tokens" in billing view (off by default).
alex: implementation gotcha — toolcall TTL on the edge is per-router; when route affinity breaks we might have two different routers each thinking they're owner. need a cross-router lease or a central coordinator. hard for private deployments.
maria: for private deployments we could expose a config: `billing.allow_remote_confirm` false by default, so private customers can opt into strict single-writer only.
opsbot: deploy-bot: started canary deploy to eng-platform-rotuefix at 1713573400 (rollout=10%).
julie: nice, track with a dashboard card: provisional vs confirmed per-minute for the canary customers. want a pre-rollout watchlist.
ben: I'll instrument the metric and add a Grafana panel. also adding a trace link to the charge events would help investigations.
samir: for code change plan: (1) make ledger writes idempotent by dedupe key; (2) add move-to-confirmed path that updates provisional rows; (3) emit telemetry on stale provisional credits; (4) add console lineage UI.
alex: sounds good. can someone take ownership of the canary eval and rollback criteria? suggested rollback if provisional_stale_count > 5 for canary orgs in 5m.
maria: i'll own canary eval and alerts. will post results in #release-war-room.
julie: and i'll scope the console patch (mockups in figma) — will link.
alex: thanks. follow-ups: samir will open PR for ledger idempotency; ben will add metrics; maria will run canary. we'll reconvene after first 2h of canary. :thumbsup:
